collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older and another villager)

collection.description: A villager who hated gardening when young now has the finest garden: laugh about it, or wonder what else might change.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, (subject.he/she) hated gardening. Hated it. Dirt, bugs, bending, waiting forever for anything to happen. Today (subject.he/she) is kneeling in (subject.his/her) garden, which is enormous, overflowing and the pride of (subject.his/her) life, and (subject.he/she) has been out here since dawn. (friend) has stopped to admire it.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I used to hate this," (subject) says. (friend) doesn't believe (subject.him/her). "You? You live out here." "I know," says (subject). "If you'd told me at twenty, I'd have thrown a squash at you." (subject.He/she) has no idea when it changed. Somewhere in the middle, the waiting started to feel like hope instead of boredom. (subject.He/she) gives (friend) a squash. Not thrown. Handed.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) wonders what else (subject.he/she) is sure about now that will change later. (subject.He/she) hates singing. (subject.He/she) hates early mornings. (subject.He/she) hates goats. Will (subject.he/she) love any of them in twenty years? (subject.He/she) looks at the nearest goat. The goat looks back. "No," says (subject). "Not you." The goat eats a lettuce.
